call_points.text: Normalised year framed as 8-9% passenger traffic growth plus 5-7% LFL, i.e. ~14-15% LFL.
Other expenses rose 22% YoY, in line with business growth excluding the lounge aggregation reclassification.
Debt-free balance sheet with ~₹9.7 bn consolidated cash as of 30 June 2026.
Chennai and Kolkata concessions come up for renewal around March 2027 and Q1FY28.
Contract renewal rate slipped to ~92% from ~94% as small highway outlets were not renewed.
International focus on Asia for now; entities set up in Dubai and Indonesia to bid for local opportunities.
No numeric FY27 revenue, margin or outlet guidance given; management only flags near-term headwinds.
Passenger traffic at TFS-managed airports rose only 1.2% in FY26 after multiple disruptions.
Q4 EBITDA margin rose 368 bps to 40.4%, helped by lower manpower spend during flight cancellations.
Q4 PAT margin fell to 26.6% from 29.1% on lower JV profit and full-year tax phasing.
Noida International Airport outlets planned to open in the first half of FY27; construction underway.
Bhogapuram International Airport operations scheduled to commence from June 2026.
Consolidated debt is nil and cash balance was ₹836 Cr as on March 31, 2026.
Q4 growth was hit by the Middle East conflict from early March; management is monitoring input costs and traffic.

operating_notes.text: Delhi T3 licence agreement is scheduled to expire on 30 September 2026.
CGST rectification order reduced tax and penalty demand to ₹14.40 Cr.
System-wide footprint at 30 June 2026 was 580 travel QSR outlets and lounges across 21 airports with 153 brands; 87 outlets and two lounges were added in the last 12 months.
Over 50 outlets are under development, mostly to open this fiscal year, with 12-18 months to normalise at existing terminals and 18-24 months at greenfield airports.
Contracts are largely minimum guarantee and/or revenue share (whichever is higher); revenue share percentages are contractually fixed for the contract life while minimum guarantees escalate.

timeline.summary: Travel Food Services Limited, via Neeta Arvind Singh, schedules Q4 & FY2026 results conference call on May 26, 2026, at 14:30 IST with Varun Kapur, Vikas Vinod Kapoor, and Chhavi Agarwal.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹460.68 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹120.8 Cr (includes ₹22.38 Cr from discontinued operations; continuing operations ₹100.22 Cr).
Travel Food Services Limited uploaded the audio recording of its Q4 FY 2025-26 earnings conference call held on May 26, 2026, at 14:30 IST.
Travel Food Services received a CGST rectification order reducing its tax and penalty demand to ₹14.40 Cr on May 27, 2026.

Varun Kapur and Karan Kapur, as promoters and authorized representatives of Kapur Family Trust, declared no encumbrance on Travel Food Services’ equity shares during FY2025-26 under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).

On its 14 August 2026 Q1FY27 call, Travel Food Services reported revenue up 20.6% YoY to ₹4.5 bn and PAT up 35.6% to ₹1.3 bn (helped by a ₹131 mn GST write-back), with EBITDA margin down to 35.8% on pre-operating costs at new airports.

watchlist.text: Shareholder approval for dividend at the ensuing AGM
EBITDA margin recovery toward prior level

watchlist.response: Management did not split the number, saying it is a blend of price, premiumisation and brand changes, and reiterated a 5-7% delta over passenger traffic.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked how much of 4.2% consolidated LFL came from higher spend per passenger versus other initiatives.

watchlist.response: CFO said returns at maturity should mimic the rest of the portfolio and the company will not chase growth without sustainable long-term profits; no numeric threshold given.
watchlist.text: Analyst pressed on the return threshold for bidding new airports and whether competitive bidding pressures returns.

watchlist.response: Management declined to give a number, calling contract wins lumpy year to year.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for a sustainable net contract gain target.

watchlist.response: CFO said roughly 8-10% of cost is fixed (occupancy, CAM charges) and the split is variable year to year; no precise figure given.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked how much of the ~50% cost base is fixed versus variable and how much grows detached from the business.
